Departmental Seminars (Colloquium) will take place six times in every semester and will be dedicated to lectures and discussions of current research and scholarship in musicology by guest speakers, department faculty, and graduate students. Participation is mandatory to BA, MA and PhD students in Musicology throughout the degree. Lectures are conducted in both English and Hebrew.
Colloquium
Departmental seminar meetings, involving undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral students as well as faculty members, will be held six times each semester. These sessions will be dedicated to student presentations, alumni talks, lectures by faculty or guest speakers, and discussions of new research and musicological literature. Participation is mandatory for all musicology students at all levels.
Class Attendance Procedure
Students must be present at every study session (class, exercise, seminar, etc.), which is set for them as part of the curriculum plan. Attendance will be checked in every class, exercise, or seminar and reported to the school secretary.
Students, who for justified reasons cannot participate in class, must notify the course teacher and the studies committee in writing of this along with the reasoning (illness, etc.).
Students who are absent from school for 14 days in a row without a sufficient and reasoned reason and/or without the approval of the school management, their studies will be terminated.
All references to the teaching committee will be through a studies committee link https://tau-ac.my.salesforce.com/.
Students who fail a course, will have to take it again in the following year and cover its full cost by themselves.
Final Exam
The final exam will be administered after the completion of all academic requirements as outlined in the program guide. The exam can be taken either in writing or orally, at the student’s discretion. The student will select a supervisor from among the department’s faculty members (all holding a PhD) and coordinate the exam content with them. A topic chosen for the final exam must not overlap with the subject of any seminar paper previously submitted by the student.
Exam Content:
Two topics must be selected:
Topic A: A theoretical issue; analysis of a research/conceptual notion; genre; portrayal of a period/era/group/style; artistic/critical/philosophical movement; historical episode, etc.
Topic B: Corpus of works: a group of works by an artist (of modest scope – not the entire œuvre); or: a group of works on a unifying theme; or: a group of works categorized by an additional characteristic (such as genre, period, style, theme, etc.).
It is recommended, though not required, to choose two interrelated topics. For example, the theoretical issue (Topic A) could be demonstrated through the selected works corpus (Topic B).
The student will prepare a bibliographic list of research, critical, and theoretical writings related to the chosen topics: approximately 200 pages for Topic A; for Topic B, excluding the works themselves, the list should cover around 120 pages. Each list must include at least five distinct items that represent significant and central research in the field of the topic; entire research books should not be selected, but rather specific chapters; electronic articles may be included (up to one per topic) if they are of proven quality.
The list will be submitted to the exam supervisor for approval. The student and the examiner will agree on a suitable date for the exam in coordination with the administration office.
Written Exam
The exam supervisor will submit the exam questions to the school’s administration office no later than one week before the scheduled exam date, with one question per topic. The exam questions will be provided to the student by the administration office on the designated date. The student must submit their answers online to the administration office within three days (72 hours). Each answer should be between seven to ten pages long, double-spaced, making the total length of the exam no more than twenty pages. Answers should reference the reading material according to academic writing standards, demonstrate mastery of the relevant bibliographic materials, and include a bibliographic list. The exam will be evaluated by the exam supervisor and an additional faculty member. If the examiner requests a hard copy, the student will be required to submit the exam in printed format.
Oral Exam
The final oral exam will be scheduled in coordination with the school’s administration office. Prior to the exam date, the examiner will prepare three questions for each of the two topics. The questions will address the central critical and interpretive issues within the topics covered. The exam will include one question per topic. The questions must be submitted to the administration office no later than one week before the exam date. The exam questions will be provided to the student by the administration office three days (72 hours) before the scheduled exam.
The oral exam will take place at the university, in the presence of the exam supervisor and an additional faculty member, and will last approximately one hour. The student may bring any relevant materials to the exam and review them during the exam session. The exam grade is final and cannot be appealed.
Graduation
Students who have completed all of the requirements for the degree and received all of the grades, must fill out the "Excursions Form - Graduates" in the "Personal Information" page.
It is the responsibility of the student to fulfill the curriculum requirements throughout the degree.
